label: BUG+DRIFT: the single-executor cli-opencode branch in deep-research-auto.yaml never resolves the OpenCode binary. It hardcodes command:'opencode' (yaml:1642) while fanout-run.cjs:2391 builds from resolveOpencodeBinary and branches on version==='v2' (fanout-run.cjs:2397); opencode-version.cjs has exactly one caller in the tree. A single-executor lineage therefore ignores OPENCODE_BIN and runs OpenCode 1 where both majors are installed, the exact configuration v4.0.0.13 was written to change. Sibling if_cli_codex does an explicit 'command -v codex' preflight, so the omission is an asymmetry not a choice. Release: v4.0.0.13. Confidence: high. Verify: grep -c resolveOpencodeBinary .skilled/commands/deep/assets/deep-research-auto.yaml -> 0.

BUG (masked by F1): the same argv block passes the OpenCode-1-only --pure flag unconditionally (yaml:1619). SKILL.md:180 says --pure is absent from OpenCode 2 run and OpenCode 1 only, and SKILL.md:266 says using it removes the entire point of cli-opencode dispatch by disabling plugins. The two defects mask each other: today the hardcoded opencode usually lands on v1 where --pure is accepted while silently stripping plugins; the moment F1 is repaired and the resolver picks OpenCode 2, the same argv carries a flag v2 run rejects, so fixing F1 alone turns a silent capability loss into a hard dispatch failure. Release: v4.0.0.13 (contradiction; flag predates it). Confidence: high. Verify: opencode2 run --help | grep -c -- --pure -> 0.

BUG: if_cli_opencode passes model:'{config.executor.model}' unguarded (yaml:1600) while its sibling if_cli_codex guards the same placeholder with '{config.executor.model}' === 'null' ? null : ... before pushing --model. The guard in the sibling proves a null model is a reachable template state, so an unset model becomes a literal '--model null' argument instead of the documented default llmgateway/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017 at variant max (SKILL.md:103), which exists only in the skill prose and not in the branch. Release: pre-v4.0.0.13 branch, unfixed by it. Confidence: medium-high (literal-null outcome depends on the substitution engine's unknown-token policy, open from iteration 8). Verify: compare sed -n '1597,1607p' and the equivalent codex block in .skilled/commands/deep/assets/deep-research-auto.yaml.

BUG: if_cli_opencode passes the working directory as --dir (yaml:1620) plus cwd to the audit wrapper, but SKILL.md:233 states OpenCode 2 takes the model's working directory from PWD, not the process directory, and a Node spawn() with cwd must also set PWD. fanout-run.cjs sets PWD; the YAML branch has no PWD handling, so the third defect in the same argv block also only fires once F1 is repaired. Release: v4.0.0.13. Confidence: medium-high. Verify: grep -n PWD .skilled/skills/system-deep-loop/runtime/scripts/fanout-run.cjs (hit) vs .skilled/commands/deep/assets/deep-research-auto.yaml (no hit).

IMPROVEMENT (duplication): the 28-entry Cursor roster exists twice, byte-identical, in executor-config.ts:353 (CURSOR_SUPPORTED_MODELS) and fanout-run.cjs:2562 (CURSOR_ALLOWED_MODELS), so v4.0.0.2's Grok 4.7 addition had to be applied twice and only the fan-out copy explains the naming quirk that grok-4.7-* carries no cursor- prefix (fanout-run.cjs:2561). Both lists agree today, release note v4.0.0.2:186 and code are aligned, and I did not find an equality assertion between them in the tests opened, so the drift is latent rather than present. Release: pre-v4, last edited by v4.0.0.2. Confidence: high for duplication, medium for 'no equality test'. Verify: diff the quoted ids of executor-config.ts:353-383 and fanout-run.cjs:2562-2592.

DRIFT (narrow): v4.0.0.16 says pi runs GPT-6.1 Terra in deep loops and fast mode sends the priority tier. Terra is on both allowlists (executor-config.ts:236, fanout-run.cjs:2623) and in the provider map (fanout-run.cjs:2850), but EXECUTOR_KIND_FLAG_SUPPORT['cli-pi'] accepts only model, reasoningEffort, timeoutSeconds and liveTools (executor-config.ts:128) while SERVICE_TIERS is a first-class type (executor-config.ts:31). Either the priority routing is encoded in the model uid as the OpenCode comment describes, and the release sentence names a uid rather than a tier field, or the behaviour is unreachable from config. Documentation-to-schema naming gap, not a proven break. Release: v4.0.0.16. Confidence: medium (pi builder argv not read). Verify: read the cli-pi builder argv in fanout-run.cjs and grep -n fast .skilled/skills/cli-external-orchestration/cli-pi/SKILL.md.
